volunteering.title: President
volunteering.description: Helped organize and spread the word about club events, like a winter get-together with ornament-making and a movie night. Handled event planning, posted on social media, and made sure everything ran smoothly so members could have a good time.

li_projects.title: Heritage — Ambition Catalyst 002
li_projects.description: Ambition Catalyst 002 consisted of 6 sessions over 2 weeks, where 25 participants developed and presented their personal projects. My initial idea was unclear. While away from home and reading a Ukrainian genealogy book, I realized I wanted to create a tool that helps people connect with their relatives through shared stories. li_projects.title: Humber Health Design Sprint 2025 — 2nd Place
li_projects.description: Worked with a great team to rethink the wellness spaces at North Campus Library; we took second place in the Health Design Sprint 2025. I had fun coming up with ideas to make the library more welcoming and helpful for all kinds of students by adding more greenery, soundproof pods for quiet time, and a cozy music area with vinyl records.

posts.text: When I was 12, I ended up moderating a homework-help website, Znanija (Brainly). I started as an active contributor in middle school, helping other students with English, Ukrainian, and literature. I still have a backpack they sent me as part of the swag bag back in 2018 👀 Peer-to-peer platforms had a certain charm. When a top answerer showed up in a thread, I knew the good grade was coming. I made a little extension for Last.fm :) The YouTube scrobblers I tried had two problems. First, they scrobble every video automatically. So, all the random videos I watched kept ending up in my Last.fm history, and I had to go back and delete them (a bit awkward 👀). Second, on videos longer than ~20 minutes, they’d start lagging. It was a pleasure connecting with designers from different backgrounds in a relaxed atmosphere this Sunday! I enjoyed my hojicha latte and chocolate croissant, too 👀 Thank you, Serhii Kyryliuk, for organizing this hangout, and I can't wait for another event!

It was a nice workshop! Much of it was familiar, which was reassuring. A few things stood out to me: • Numbers in the resume bullet points. I spent most of my Service Design class looking at digital wireframes and sticky notes on whiteboards. But this Saturday, I experienced my first "service safari" in the wild at the Service Design Drinks Toronto walk through Vale of Avoca and Moore Park Ravine. It was a pleasure meeting Sharmeena Lalloo, Anna Kylymchuk, Elfine Caumont, Karthik Jambunathan, Den Roman, Stephanie C., and many other talented people. Do you find mock interviews awkward? Me too. For the past month, I’ve been meeting weekly with other product designers to prep for my Summer co-op interviews. I led our first session about portfolios, and since then, we’ve been going through different parts of the design interview process as a group. You don't need to spend 20 minutes manually applying to a job posting... So happy to be the president of Humber UX Society this year! There are already 20 members, and we haven't even scheduled an event yet. Stay tuned for what's coming next :)

I had an amazing time at the Ambition Housewarming. A lot of new faces and some familiar ones, back from Catalyst in August (but that’s a topic for a different post...) Hope to see what everyone is up to at the documentary premiere on the 30th!
